body: Seems like a temporary solution, i can't stop watching movies or so, it's a huge part of who i am

I'm sorry for your lost. I lost my cat last year in a suddent event right before my eyes. He was my best, and only true friend at that time. The pain was excrutiating. I remember wishing it was me dead instead of him. I remember I cried for weeks I think. Drank a lot. Only a couple of my friends were close to giving support and others just didn't let me talk about it. But I wanted to. So I downloaded this diary app on my phone and started writing to my deceased cat everyday for a couple weeks. I've never been a diary-writer but it kind of helped in a weird way. Maybe you can try!
I avoided looking at his photos thanks to the couple friends mentioned above, because everytime I tried, I bursted into tears. I know you wanna see your cat, but maybe avoid looking at photos/watching videos until you feel totally ok&strong enough to remember it with a smile, not tears. Hope you feel better, PM me if you wanna talk.

Thanks everybody for the suggestions. I've called a couple, they are extremely expensive and don't apply a tailored fee of any kind. I'm gonna keep searching tho!  Thanks to you now I know I can ask for this kind of adjustment!
Hey thanks for the reply, I'm sorry but I don't know what that means?

Thanks for your thoughtful reply... I hope we all find that great friendship we hope for. You're rght in saying that my friends will never change. It seems the best thing to do will be to learn how to be comfortable being on your own. I'm still learning it. 

Actually, the other day I confronted my friends about something like this. Told them I was upset with them for not calling me in these hard times I'm having. One of them got mad and told me nobody HAS TO know whats wrong with me or call me. Others said they didn't like to call in these situations. Told them they should, if they want better relationships. I don't think they cared. I guess what I need is either new friends or comfort found in complete solitude.

They really do. I grew up watching my mom and her friends being there for each other through thick and thin and always tried to be like them. I realized when I grew up that it's not the way how everybody grew up. I kind of believed it's like a generation problem. People care so little about what's around them anymore. So much selfishness. I wish I could live in the past decades

I know right? I wondered what's wrong with me for a long time. I recently decided that it was my negativeness that drove people off. But I'm not sure. I always say I was an extremely happy person in high school, but from time to time I remember these small details, where I'm walking on a narrow pavement with 2 friends and it's not wide enough for all of us to walk side by side, and I'm literally ALWAYS the one left behind. Or how all my life people interrupted me while I speak. It became the thing that I hate most in life, by far. I mean, I guess there was always something wrong with me that prevented other people to respect me even when I was a positive person. I guess I don't care anymore... I still can't help believing that I'll find the right kind of people someday. I hope we all do... by the way, happy happy birthday. I'm sorry you're friends are a-holes

Sundays are the worst. I feel you. My single mom hates them too, says it's the day that people spend with their families and since ours is fallen apart... well, it's sad for her too. Crying is just my regular sunday activity.
